name: El Dorado State Park (Bemis Creek)
note: Bemis Creek area of El Dorado State Park (KDWP), a small peninsula on the lake's east arm entered straight off K-177, about 2 km south of the Bluestem Point turn-off: 24 gravel sites inside one loop ringed by trees. KDWP files it under its Bluestem Point area, which is its own entry. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: campitks.gov (2026-11-06): the 'Bemis Creek' loop filter on parkID 519119 lists 24 sites (515-538), all 'Standard with Water and Electric Hookups', site-specific reservable, gravel, 'Maximum Vehicle Length: 70', 8 'Driveway Entry: Pull-Through'; KDWP's Bemis Creek Camping Area page (search snippet, 2026-11-06) gives 24 water/electric reservable sites, and the agency's per-site photos show developed gravel RV pads. A separate place from 2092 Bluestem Point: OSM has its own service road leaving K-177 at 37.85016,-96.74938 into the loop (Esri imagery agrees), while Bluestem Point Road meets K-177 about 2 km north; Big Pine, the nearest Bluestem loop, is 1.8 km west across the water, and 15622 Shady Creek (Patriot Lane) is 1.4 km southwest on its own road. Public campground, no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: Esri World Imagery with campitks' per-site GIS coordinates plotted (2026-11-06): all 24 pads sit inside the campground's own perimeter loop road, and a mostly continuous tree belt lines the shore outside that road. The closest pads are 45-65 m from El Dorado Lake: 519-521 on the south side, 522/523 at the west tip and 532-535 on the north side. The loop road and the trees lie between them and the water, so the campground is not lakefront. The view is filtered: campitks' official site photos for 524, 525, 526, 527 and 537 show open lake through scattered trees, and campitks marks every site 'River/Lake View: Y' -> lakeview. Not below the dam: the pads' DEM is 412 m against 407 m on the open water nearby, and the dam is about 5 km west.

fees.note: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus $13 a night for two utilities (water and electric), so every Bemis Creek site costs $30.75 a night. All 24 are designated prime sites, which adds $2 a night on stays April-September ($32.75). A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. Water and electric shows as electric +$11 plus water +$2. Read 2026-10-15.

fees_source: https://ksoutdoors.gov/licenses-permits-fees/kansas-state-park-entrance-and-camping-fees (as quoted on sibling 2092: 'Daily Camping Permit ... $12.75 per night $17.75 per night'; 'Utility Fees ... $13.00 per night for two utilities'; 'Prime Site Fee ... designated sites on stays April 1-September 30 ... $2.00 per night'; 'a $2.75 processing fee will apply to each camping stay'; 'Daily Vehicle Permit ... $5.00 $7.00'), read 2026-10-15 for 2092; the fee shape is copied from 2092. Every Bemis Creek site is 'Number of Utilities: 2' and 'Prime Site: Y' on campitks campsiteDetails, read 2026-11-06.

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

booking.note: Sites are reserved site by site on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov). The reservation window shown on 2026-11-06 ran from Nov 7, 2026 to Dec 6, 2027. Self-registration on arrival is also allowed. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.

booking_source: https://www.campitks.gov/camping/eldorado-state-park/r/campgroundDetails.page?parkID=519119 (park-wide '2027 CAMPSITES Holiday Minimum Stay Rule' and '14 days maximum consecutive stay rule', as recorded on 2092 2026-11-06) and campsiteDetails for all 24 Bemis Creek sites (siteID 6206-6229: 'Site Reserve Type: Site-Specific', 'Self Reg Allowed: Y', 'Reservation Window: Sat Nov 07 2026 - Mon Dec 06 2027'), read 2026-11-06
flags: hookups: electric 50, water true, sewer absent (no Sewer Hookup attribute on any site, so it is not stamped as false) - campitks campsiteDetails, all 24 sites 'Electricity Hookup: 50/30/20', 'Water Hookup: Y', read 2026-11-06; KDWP's El Dorado SP PDF (search snippet) also names Bemis Creek among the 50-amp loops

sites: count 24, max_rig_ft 70, pull_through true (8 pull-through 524-531, 16 back-in), surface gravel, max vehicle width 20, up to 3 vehicles - campitks campsiteDetails (all 24 sites), read 2026-11-06

booking: reservable site-specific on campitks (ReserveAmerica), self-reg Y, window ~13 months (Nov 7 2026 - Dec 6 2027), max stay 14, 2027 holiday 3-night minimum - campitks campgroundDetails + campsiteDetails, read 2026-11-06
season: year_round true - campitks campgroundDetails 'Open year round.' (park-wide, as on 2092), and the Bemis Creek sites take bookings from Nov 7 2026 on, read 2026-11-06

facilities: flush_toilets true, vault_toilets true - campitks campsiteDetails at every Bemis Creek site ('Modern Restrooms: Within 1/4 Mile', 'Vault Toilet: Within 1/4 Mile'), read 2026-11-06. Showers are NOT stamped: every site says 'Shower House with Restrooms: Outside Facility', unlike Bluestem's 'Within 1/4 Mile'.

KDWP files Bemis Creek under its Bluestem Point area (its page URL is .../Areas/Bluestem-Point/Bemis-Creek-Camping-Area), but Bluestem's own counts on the park page (197 water/electric = Fishermans Point 53 + Quail Run 56 + Big Pine 88) leave out Bemis Creek's 24. It is a separate entry here because it has its own entrance off K-177 and is 1.8 km from the nearest Bluestem loop. 2092 does not need to absorb its count.

The ksoutdoors.gov Bemis Creek page returned 403 to direct fetches and the Wayback Machine rate-limited me (429), so the KDWP page is cited from its search-result snippet (24 water/electric, reservable) only.

Side finding for 13955 Boulder Bluff (not changed): on campitks (2026-11-06) its Pintail Loop and Equestrian Loop list 56 sites: 22 water/electric at 50/30/20 A, 33 primitive and 1 shelter, all 30-ft back-ins. That roughly matches KDWP's 'Boulder Bluff ... Water, Electric: 24', so KDWP's 24 there is Boulder Bluff's own and not Bemis Creek's.
